caveat.ca-credit-2025-figures: These limits and amounts are for tax year 2025. The 2026 figures are not final yet and may be different.
caveat.calfresh-mixed-status: If some people in your home are not eligible because of immigration status, others in your home may still get food benefits. The amount depends on who in your home is eligible.
caveat.calfresh-work-student-rules: This check does not include work rules or student rules. Some adults 18 to 64 with no child under 14 at home must work or train 80 hours a month to keep benefits after 3 months. College students have extra rules.
caveat.eitc-estimate: The amount is an estimate. It assumes all your income is from work. The IRS table may be a few dollars different.
caveat.eitc-refund-rule-proposed: A proposed federal rule may change who can get this credit as a refund, starting with 2026 returns. It would affect people who are not U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or qualified noncitizens. The rule is not final.
caveat.energy-account-rules: Utilities have more rules, such as the bill being in your name. Your utility makes the final decision.
caveat.lifeline-one-per-household: Only one LifeLine discount is allowed per home, on either a home phone or a cell phone.

pack.us-ca.name: California and federal programs
program.ca-lifeline.apply: Apply through a participating phone company or the California LifeLine Administrator.
program.ca-lifeline.documents: Usually: proof that someone in the household is in a qualifying program, or proof of income such as a tax return or pay stubs.
program.ca-lifeline.name: California LifeLine phone discount
program.ca-lifeline.office: California LifeLine Administrator, a program of the California Public Utilities Commission
program.ca-lifeline.renewal: Eligibility is renewed every year. One discount per household.
program.ca-lifeline.summary: A monthly discount on home phone or cell phone service for households that qualify by income or by taking part in certain public programs.
program.caleitc.apply: Claim it on the California tax return with form FTB 3514.
program.caleitc.documents: Usually: a Social Security number or ITIN for everyone on the return, Forms W-2 with California wages, and records of self-employment income.
program.caleitc.name: California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC)
program.caleitc.renewal: It is claimed again each year on the state tax return.
program.caleitc.summary: A California tax credit for people who work and earn under the state limit. It lowers the state tax owed and can be paid as a refund.
program.calfresh.apply: Apply online at BenefitsCal.com, by phone, or at the county social services office. An interview usually follows.
program.calfresh.documents: Usually: proof of income from the last 30 days and proof of identity. Rent, utility and child care costs can help.
program.calfresh.name: CalFresh food benefits
program.calfresh.office: Your county social services office, under the California Department of Social Services
program.calfresh.renewal: Benefits are approved for a set period and must be renewed before it ends.
program.calfresh.summary: Monthly food benefits loaded on an EBT card. CalFresh is California's name for the federal SNAP program.
program.care.apply: Apply with your gas or electric utility. The form is short and is usually online.
program.care.documents: Usually only the utility account in your name. The utility may ask for proof of income or of a qualifying program later.
program.care.name: CARE energy bill discount
program.care.office: Your gas or electric utility; the program is overseen by the California Public Utilities Commission
program.care.renewal: The utility asks you to renew from time to time.
program.care.summary: A discount on gas and electric bills for households under the income limit or taking part in certain public programs.
program.federal-eitc.apply: Claim it on the federal tax return (Form 1040). Free IRS-certified volunteer sites can prepare the return.
program.federal-eitc.documents: Usually: Social Security cards for everyone on the return, birth dates, Forms W-2 and 1099 or other records of income.
program.federal-eitc.name: Federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
program.federal-eitc.renewal: It is claimed again each year on the tax return.
program.federal-eitc.summary: A federal tax credit for people who work and have low to moderate income. It lowers the tax owed and can be paid as a refund.
program.fera.apply: Apply with your electric utility (PG&E, SCE or SDG&E).
program.fera.documents: Usually only the electric account in your name. The utility may ask for proof of income later.
program.fera.name: FERA electric bill discount
program.fera.office: Your electric utility; the program is overseen by the California Public Utilities Commission
program.fera.renewal: The utility asks you to renew from time to time.
program.fera.summary: A discount on electric bills for households whose income is just above the CARE limit.
program.yctc.apply: Claim it on the California tax return with form FTB 3514.
program.yctc.documents: Usually: a Social Security number or ITIN for you and the child under 6, and records of earned income.
program.yctc.name: Young Child Tax Credit
program.yctc.renewal: It is claimed again each year on the state tax return.
program.yctc.summary: A California tax credit for families with a child under 6, claimed together with the California Earned Income Tax Credit.
question.ageGroup.help: Your age at the end of the year. If you file a joint tax return, choose 25 to 64 if either of you is 25 to 64.
question.ageGroup.label: How old are you?
question.benefits.help: Choose all that apply. Choose none if no one does.
question.benefits.label: Does anyone in your home get any of these?
question.calfreshEligibleMember.help: Some others also count, such as children under 18 with a green card, Cuban or Haitian entrants, and citizens of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands, or Palau.
question.calfreshEligibleMember.label: Is at least one person in your home a U.S. citizen, or a green card holder for 5 years or more?
question.energyProvider.help: If you are not sure, look at the top of your bill.
question.energyProvider.label: Who sends your gas or electric bill?
question.filingStatus.help: Pick the status you expect to use for this year's return.
question.filingStatus.label: How will you file your tax return?
question.hasChildUnder6.label: Is any of your children under 6 at the end of the year?
question.hasEarnedIncome.label: Did you earn money from a job or your own business this year?
question.hasElderlyOrDisabledMember.labe: Is anyone in your home 60 or older, or living with a disability?
question.householdSize.help: Count everyone who lives with you and shares food or bills.
question.householdSize.label: How many people live in your home, including you?
question.housing.label: Do you rent or own your home?
question.income.help: Before taxes. A range is enough for now.
question.income.label: About how much does your household earn in a year?
question.investmentIncome.label: About how much did you get this year from interest, dividends, or other investments?
question.numQualifyingChildren.help: Count children who lived with you more than half the year and are under 19 (under 24 if a full-time student, any age if disabled). Count only children who have a Social Security number.
question.numQualifyingChildren.label: How many children can you claim on your tax return?
question.taxIdType.help: If you file a joint return, answer for the person whose number has more limits.
question.taxIdType.label: What kind of tax ID number do you have?
exception.caleitc.filing-status: Married filing separately can still qualify when a child you claim lived with you more than half the year and you lived apart from your spouse for the last 6 months of the year, or are legally separated.
exception.federal-eitc.filing-status: Married filing separately can still qualify when a child you claim lived with you more than half the year and you lived apart from your spouse for the last 6 months of the year, or are legally separated.
exception.yctc.filing-status: Married filing separately can still qualify when a child you claim lived with you more than half the year and you lived apart from your spouse for the last 6 months of the year, or are legally separated.
